name: Aetherion Ascendancy
startIntroPart1: Beyond the dying stars, the Aetherion Ascendancy mastered matter, memory and war. Its fleets crossed the void not in search of survival, but dominion.
startIntroPart2: Archon Nyra Voss, the Continuum has opened a path into a younger world. Will you guide Aetherion to unquestioned supremacy and forge an empire that outlives the stars?
declaringWar: Your future has been calculated. It ends beneath our shadow.
attacked: You have mistaken restraint for weakness. The correction will be absolute.
defeated: The Continuum fractures, but our signal will cross eternity.
denounced: Your accusation has been recorded among the final errors of your age.
declaringFriendship: Stand beside us, and history may remember your name.
introduction: I am Archon Nyra Voss. Speak clearly; the Ascendancy has little use for hesitation.
hateHello: You are consuming time that no longer belongs to you.
tradeRequest: This exchange benefits you more than you understand.
uniqueText: Absolute power fantasy: 99,999 Food, Gold, Culture and Faith per city each turn; nearly free purchases; one-turn construction and tile improvements; 9,999-fold resources; ascendant religion; devastating armies and map-spanning movement.

civilopediaText.text: The Aetherion Ascendancy is an original science-fiction civilization created for players who want a deliberately unbalanced power fantasy.
Its cities complete normal construction in one turn, can purchase almost anything, ignore occupation unhappiness and turn every acquired tradable resource into 9,999 times its normal quantity.
Every Aetherion military unit receives overwhelming combat strength, fifty extra movement and extended sight, allowing armies to cross huge portions of the map in a single turn.
Aetherion workers complete ordinary tile improvements in one turn, while Genesis Gardens and Continuum Spires produce impossible yields from individual tiles.
Continuum Ascendance is the civilization's favored religion and unlocks original beliefs built around infinite wealth, growth, culture, faith and religious pressure.
